reasoning: Starmer has a commanding Commons majority and faces no election until 2029. Historical data shows prime ministers rarely leave office within the first 18 months of a full term unless there is a severe scandal or health crisis, both of which are low-probability tail events. The market-implied 11.2% appears to overprice these risks given the current stability.
evidence_points: Labour holds a 170+ seat majority, making a successful no-confidence vote or internal coup extremely unlikely.
No UK prime minister since Eden (1955) has left office within 13 months of a fresh general-election victory without an extraordinary event like Truss's market meltdown.
Starmer’s approval ratings are weak but not catastrophic, and there is no active leadership challenge.
